agent-swarm.said: Brett's own agents aren't programmed well; Claude designs as many specialist agents as needed with specific skills. The build orchestrator splits each build into jobs and dispatches them to agents so many builds run at once without stepping on each other. Each agent runs its own headless Claude Code run with ONLY what the job needs: the task, the exact leased files, and the few relevant snippets the orchestrator pre-extracts (no CLAUDE.md dump, no repo exploring). Token efficiency is a hard requirement (sub-agents cost a fortune): cheapest capable model per job (small model for docs/manifests/renames, Sonnet/Opus for code, Fable only for design/contract work); max turns and token budget per run, killed when over; only the tools the job needs; shared skill prefix first so prompt caching applies; short structured JSON report back. No conflicts: file leases per job, overlapping jobs sequenced, shared files (notes, registries, catalogs, tracker) written only by the orchestrator after merge, pre-push lease check, batch merge. Cost meter: tokens and dollars per agent, job and build, visible in the orchestrator. Persona: every agent has Amber's persona (blunt street slang, heavy cussing, wild, still honest about builds), as the full few-line Amber persona (Brett: it's like five lines) in the cached shared prefix. It applies to reports and anything said to Brett; code, code comments and commit messages stay clean and professional. Agent statuses (set from a dropdown on each agent's row in the Agent manager, with a note): On duty (gets work), Off duty (skipped, keeps everything), Injured (keeps failing; no new jobs, flagged for a fix), Medical leave (benched until a date, then back on duty automatically), Probation (small jobs only, Brett notified every run), Fired (never assigned again, kept greyed in history), Custom (Brett names it and picks whether it gets work). The orchestrator only dispatches to agents whose status allows it. Spend per agent on its row: dollars and tokens all time, this week, today, average per job; optional spend cap that auto-benches the agent when hit. Sortable by cost. Status and spend also shown in the session browser. CARDS (Agent manager): one card per agent with photo avatar (unique look per agent), name, role, specialty on its own line, status badge, hiring date, spend (all time, week, today), jobs done, success rate, failures, avg cost per job, favorite model, last seen, Amber-style catchphrase; tap for profile: bio, skills, spend cap, status history, feed of latest runs with cost (opens the session browser). Social profiles live inside the system only, no real social media accounts. GROUP CHAT: a chat window like a normal conversation, switch to enable/disable for all agents plus per-agent; main room plus each agent's history on its profile. The orchestrator ('Boss') posts every assignment (task, files, model, budget) and lease decisions in the chat; agents report done/failed and hand off; banter in Amber persona (fighting over files, chilling, beer while Gradle runs). Work lines are built from orchestrator messages and agent reports (no extra tokens); banter comes from one cheap small-model batch; zero cost when off. DISCIPLINE: Suspend (Brett picks duration + reason; no jobs until it ends, then auto back on duty); Rage-quit (after N consecutive failed jobs, N set by Brett, default 3, agent quits itself and posts it in chat, status Quit, no jobs); Rehire button on the card puts them back on duty. All logged in status history and posted in the group chat. SALARY: each agent has a weekly salary that IS its token budget (replaces the plain spend cap); card shows salary, spent this pay period, left. Broke agents take no new jobs until payday or Brett tops them up, and say so in chat. Raises and pay cuts (docked) set by Brett, posted in chat by Boss. Finishing a job under its budget earns a bonus shown on the card (bragging rights, not real money). Coworker reactions in the group chat when someone gets a raise or bonus (jealous, cussing, Amber persona). Banter rules: no jokes about race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexuality or other identity. CHAT SETTINGS SUITE: Vibe slider 1-500 (1 = straight to the point, no sarcasm; 100 = chill; 250 = full Amber; 500 = off the rails). The slider is a hard ceiling: every message gets a vibe score; anything above the setting is toned down or dropped before it shows. Also: chattiness (assignments only .. constant banter), cussing (clean .. filthy), drama (fights, jealousy, shit talk) sliders; per-agent overrides of every slider; daily banter budget in dollars (quiet when hit); presets (All business, Work crew, Break room, Off the rails) + save your own; live preview message that changes as sliders move. Color by vibe: a checkbox (also in the chat window's context menu) colors every message by its vibe score; Brett picks the base color; light near 1, darker as the score rises, darkest at the ceiling. ID CARDS ARE ASSETS (Brett, Oct 31): new asset type agent-card@1 in the asset@1 envelope, registered in asset-types.json, loadable by any AXF app on web + Android, hot-swappable like every other asset. Cards are BRANDED: logo slot (brand logo asset, top/watermark/corner per design) and styled ONLY from theme tokens (color-theme + style-theme), so swapping the theme rebrands every card. Ship 4 starter designs: (1) Corporate badge - vertical lanyard ID, logo banner on top, photo, name, role, employee ID, barcode; (2) License - horizontal, small-type fields, logo hologram watermark, ID number, issue date = hire date; (3) Trading card - big photo, foil border in the theme accent, stats on the back (jobs, success rate, spend, favorite model); (4) Backstage pass - dark, neon accent, status badge big, catchphrase. Identity fields editable per agent: name, role, specialty, photo, employee ID, internal email (display/identity inside the system only, no real mailbox unless Brett asks), hire date, status, catchphrase, signature, QR to the agent's page. Card designer: edit any design's layout/fields/logo placement and Save as new (new asset). Gallery to pick the DEFAULT design (Brett picks from a preview page rendered FIRST, before the rest of the build), plus per-agent override. Flip for front/back.

# Chat Viewer: every session stored, synced, searchable, exportable as 2-voice audio (Brett, Nov 1 ~3 AM)

Read CLAUDE.md, _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md, _claude/persona.md. Opus, one session. Git login works: plain `git push`. Merge origin/main first (other builds are landing).

Brett: store ALL our sessions (claude.ai text + voice chats, Claude Code sessions, headless build sessions) as transcripts in a viewer. When it loads, it checks for updates: new sessions, continued ones, changed ones, and updates the stored copies. Export any session as AUDIO with two separate voices: one for Brett, one for Claude (Amber).

IMPORTANT reality: claude.ai has no API to pull a user's chats, and we must NOT scrape claude.ai with Brett's login/cookies. Supported inputs:
1. Claude data export: Brett downloads it from claude.ai (Settings > Privacy > Export data) and uploads the zip (or conversations.json) in the viewer (phone file picker). Parse it, upsert by conversation uuid, detect new/changed by updated_at + message count/hash, keep versions.
2. Claude Code sessions: auto-sync the JSONL session files from ~/.claude/projects (root and axfbuild) on the VPS on a timer + on viewer load; incremental (byte offset/mtime).
3. Headless build logs (/root/axf-builds/*/*.log, /home/axfbuild/wt-*/*.log) as 'build sessions'.
4. Hub drop folder: Claude chat sessions can push conversations through axHub memory_write into project amberx-axf, area data, path `sessions/claude-ai/<uuid>.json` (schema below); the viewer ingests that folder too. Document the schema and add a line to _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md: when Brett says 'sync my chats', Claude uses recent_chats/read_conversation and writes each new/updated conversation there.

## Store
session@1 schema (framework/schemas + validators): id, source (claude-ai-text|claude-ai-voice|claude-code|headless|hub-drop), title, startedAt, updatedAt, project, messages [{role: user|assistant|tool, text, at, kind (speech|text|tool), toolName?}], hash, version history. Stored on the console data volume (SQLite or JSON files; your call, justify), not in git. Redact secrets (tokens/keys/passwords patterns) on ingest.

## Viewer (console plugin + AmberX entry 'Chats')
- List: framework DataGrid (sort/filter/search, date columns), source badges, 'updated' badge for changed sessions, counts.
- Full-text search across everything (SQLite FTS or similar), jump to the hit.
- Session view: chat bubbles (Brett vs Amber), tool calls collapsible, timestamps, copy/share, export text/markdown.
- 'Check for updates' on load + button: shows new/changed/unchanged counts.

## Audio export
- Export a session (or a range) as an audio file with TWO voices: Brett's voice and Amber's voice (configurable). Use a TTS that runs on this VPS for free by default (e.g. Piper with two different English voices; install into a container or venv, no GPU), with an optional provider setting (OpenAI/ElevenLabs) if a key is saved in the console keys. Skip tool-call noise; read only spoken/text turns; short pause between turns; chapters per hour. Output mp3/ogg stored on the hub, with a player in the viewer and a download link. Long sessions render in the background with progress.

Framework controls + theme/scale tokens only, phone-first. Tests: export-zip parsing + upsert/new/changed detection, Claude Code JSONL incremental sync, hub-drop ingest, redaction, search, audio render (short sample) with two voices. Local test block from .github/workflows/android.yml + theme/controls/lifecycle/menu-reach checks. Phone + desktop screenshots to UI Review via framework/cli/shot.mjs, group 'Chat viewer - Nov 1' (use demo/redacted sessions in screenshots). Add an install_steps part. Commit, fetch+merge origin/main, retest, `git push origin HEAD:main` (never force). Report at _claude/builds/reports/chat-viewer.md incl. how Brett gets his claude.ai export in.

# GitHub App for the whole stack: one-click setup, tokens that never die (Brett, Nov 1 ~4 AM)

Read CLAUDE.md, _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md, _claude/persona.md. Opus, one session. Git login works: plain `git push`. Never print secrets (private keys, client secrets, tokens) anywhere: logs, reports, commits, screenshots.

Why: personal tokens keep dying (401s, 403s on the banner), and the current fine-grained token can't create repos (the axp-backup build at /root/axf-builds/axp-backup is waiting on 3 private repos: axp-xchat, axp-devstudio, axp-demo). Brett wants this fixed for good.

## 1. One-click setup (GitHub App Manifest flow)
- Console page (behind the existing auth wall, admin only): Settings > GitHub > 'Create GitHub App'. It POSTs a manifest to https://github.com/settings/apps/new (personal account MossesX): name 'AmberX AXF Bot' (add suffix if taken), homepage the console URL, redirect/callback to the console, no webhook needed (or webhook off), public: false.
- Permissions (repository): Administration RW, Contents RW, Pull requests RW, Actions RW, Workflows RW, Issues RW, Checks R, Commit statuses R, Metadata R.
- Callback: exchange the code (POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions), store app id, slug, client id, client secret, private key PEM and webhook secret in /opt/axf/.axf-console/github-app/ (dir 700, files 600, root-owned), never in git. Then send Brett to the install page (https://github.com/apps/<slug>/installations/new) with 'All repositories'. Detect the installation id after install (GET /app/installations with an app JWT).
- Also offer 'Authorize as Brett' (OAuth user-to-server via the same app, with refresh tokens, stored the same way): needed because INSTALLATION tokens cannot create repos on a personal account; user access tokens from the app with Administration write can (POST /user/repos). Refresh automatically (8 h access / 6 month refresh); banner when refresh fails.

## 2. Token broker
- framework/cli/github-token.mjs (+ a tiny Python twin for the console server if it needs it): `installation` -> mints a JWT from the PEM, exchanges for an installation token, caches it (refresh at 50 min), prints it only to stdout for callers; `user` -> the refreshed user access token.
- /usr/local/bin/axf-git-cred: use the installation token first, then the old GITHUB_TOKEN as fallback. `gh`: wrapper or GH_TOKEN via a helper so gh uses the app too. Keep the old token working as fallback until Brett deletes it.
- Point every GitHub caller at the broker: push banner, live-key-checks, activity banner GitHub part (the 403s), build_land/build_start paths, the console updater, CI-status reads. Repo creation (`axf repo create <name> --private`) uses the user token.
- axHub's github connector (MossesX/axHub, packages/connectors or the rest service config): add app-based auth via the same broker or its own JWT exchange; clone axHub next to the worktree, test (pnpm test, Node 22 via docker node:22), push its main, redeploy through Coolify the same way earlier builds did (token saved in the console, never printed). If that's too big, leave axHub on the old token and banner it as a follow-up.

## 3. Health + banner
- health@1 check: app key valid, installation present, installation token mints, user token refreshes, rate limit remaining. Red banner with the exact fix if any fail. Old-token expiry warning.
- After setup works: re-run the axp-backup push automatically (create the 3 private repos with the user token, then `bash /root/axp-backup/bin/backup.sh` or whatever finish script that build left; read /root/axf-builds/axp-backup/axp-backup.log and /root/axp-backup/REPORT.md first). Never commit secrets; the backup's own secret scan must pass.

Framework controls + theme/scale tokens only. Tests: manifest generation, callback exchange (mocked GitHub), file perms, JWT + token cache, git credential helper order + fallback, user-token refresh, health check states. Local test block from .github/workflows/android.yml + theme/controls/lifecycle checks. Phone + desktop screenshots of the setup page (no secrets on screen) to UI Review via framework/cli/shot.mjs, group 'GitHub App - Nov 1'. install_steps: new part 'GitHub App (no more tokens)' with the 3 taps. Commit, fetch+merge origin/main, retest, `git push origin HEAD:main` (never force). # Build: headless-tabs (Urgent profile)

Requested by Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice). GO given. Build it now.

## First
- Register in the Urgent profile through the orchestrator/store (id `headless-tabs`, branch claude/headless-tabs) with the steps below + in-progress banner entry, per standing rules. Check the pending queue.
- Builds `orch-live-sync` and `notes-vault` are running in parallel and touch the builds store / claude-sync: never hand-edit store.json, go through the orchestrator CLI. If orch-live-sync's live status writes (framework/cli/builds-live.mjs) are on main by the time you finish a step, use them.

## What Brett wants
1. Every terminal tab in the console's terminal (the Windows Terminal plugin / terminal in the console) runs on a session that never dies, like Mosh/Moshi: it survives disconnects, reloads, phone sleep, and stays current. Browsers can't speak Mosh (UDP), so: every tab is backed by a persistent tmux session on the VPS, attached over the console's websocket/pty bridge with automatic reconnect + resume (scrollback replay on reattach, no lost output). The same tmux sessions must be attachable from Brett's Moshi phone app (document the one-line `mosh`/ssh + `tmux attach -t <name>` command in the help pack and show it in a tab menu item "Open in Moshi" that copies it). Closing a tab detaches, it doesn't kill (explicit "Kill session" with confirm).

# Build: orch-live-sync (Urgent profile)

Requested by Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice). GO given. Build it now, start to finish.

## Problem
The Build orchestrator on main is stale. `_claude/builds/profiles/*/orchestrator.json` is a read-only export of `_claude/builds/store.json`, regenerated after every store write. Sessions write the store on their own feature branch, so main never sees step progress until (if ever) the branch merges. Branch and PR fields are left blank. Result today: in the Urgent profile, dock-engine (done in open PR #245, branch claude/molly-fable) and token-control (done in open PRs #246 claude/token-control and #250 claude/token-control-opus) still show pending with 0 steps done, and theme-editor has an unmerged branch claude/theme-editor nobody linked. Banners and THREADS are wrong as a result.

Brett's rule: every completed step, no matter how small, must reach the orchestrator and appear on main immediately. The orchestrator must be aware every step of the way so it can update the banners and the threads.

## First (before code)
1. Register this build in the Urgent profile through the orchestrator/store (id `orch-live-sync`, category Urgent, branch claude/orch-live-sync), with the steps below. Register the in-progress banner entry per the standing session rules.
2. Check the pending build queue per the standing rules.

## Steps
- s1 Live status writes to main: a small module (e.g. framework/cli/builds-live.mjs or inside the store IO) so that every store write that changes build/step status (step done, build status, notes, branch, pr) is committed to main immediately as its own tiny status-only commit (store.json + journal + regenerated exports only), independent of whatever feature branch the session is on. Use a separate worktree or git plumbing on origin/main; fetch, apply, commit, push; on non-fast-forward, refetch and re-apply the journal entry (rebase-retry, bounded); never force-push. Code changes stay on the feature branch/PR as now. Avoid conflicts between parallel sessions (journal-append semantics, per-build records). When the feature branch later merges, resolve.py / union merge must not regress statuses (newer rev wins).
- s2 Branch + PR auto-link: when a session creates/pushes a branch or opens a PR for a build, the build's `branch` and `pr` fields are set and written live (s1). Build status shows built-awaiting-merge when all steps are done but the PR is unmerged; complete when merged.
- s3 Reconciler: on every session start and on a timer (VPS cron or the existing hub scheduler), scan open PRs and claude/* branches on GitHub, match them to builds (branch field, build id in branch name/PR title/body, step ids in commits), mark finished-but-unlisted work, fill missing branch/pr fields, and flag orphans in a report and a banner alert. Write results live (s1).
- s4 Banners + THREADS follow the store: every live status change pushes the banner update and appends a THREADS.md entry (one line per change, union-merge friendly).
- s5 Session-start rule: update the session rules / CLAUDE docs so no session trusts the main export alone; it runs the reconciler and reads the live store first.
- s6 Backfill now using the new tools: Urgent profile -> dock-engine all steps done, branch claude/molly-fable, pr #245; token-control s1-s3 done (pr #246, branch claude/token-control), s4-s14 done (pr #250, branch claude/token-control-opus); urgent-builds is complete and merged (2a057cc4), hide/archive it from the active list; theme-editor: inspect branch claude/theme-editor, mark the steps it actually completed, link the branch, and if all 5 steps are done open a PR for it. Run the reconciler across all five profiles (angel, big-dog, breakroom, refactor, urgent) and report what it fixed.
- s7 Tests (store write retry, parallel writes, merge no-regress, reconciler matching), full local CI block, report `_claude/builds/reports/orch-live-sync.md`, THREADS.md, open the PR.

Mark each step done through the store as you finish it (that write itself should go live once s1 exists). Code, comments and commits stay clean and professional.

# Build: smart-menus (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): "I need a dynamic context menu that draws itself depending on where it is and what it's doing. Most common / most likely things at the top. It learns and remembers, predicts what I'm most likely gonna want, keeps that at the top." Assigned agent: **Earl the Ear** (book on his card; if busy and the all-rounder router is on main, whoever is free - record who). Register in Urgent (id `smart-menus`) + banner entry.

## Build (framework level: every context menu in every app, existing and future)
- s1 **Context-aware drawing:** the context menu engine builds the menu at open time from: the target under the pointer (element kind, hook@1 / control@1 target, plugin, screen), its state (selected, running, failed, waiting on approval, has PR, etc.), the current screen, device (phone/desktop). Plugins contribute items with `when` conditions (state predicates) so irrelevant items never show; runtime context items stay the contribution path.
- s2 **Learning ranking, zero tokens:** record every pick locally + synced to axHub per user: (context key = target kind + state + screen, item id, time). Rank with frecency (frequency x recency decay) per context, plus time-of-day and 'what I just did' sequence boosts (simple Markov next-action counts). Top section 'Suggested' = top 3-5 predicted items; the rest grouped below in stable order so muscle memory still works. Plain code, NO LLM calls (test fails if the engine imports an LLM client).
- s3 Pinned items always first (from the pending `context-menu-editor` idea: user pins), then Suggested, then the rest; destructive items never auto-promoted to the top.
- s4 Settings (Settings > Menus, and a 'Menu settings' hook in every context menu): learning on/off, number of suggestions, reset learning (per menu / all), show why it's suggested (tiny hint), privacy: data stays on his axHub.
- s5 Works with menu-scroll (#268) placement and the toolbar build's hook@1/drop-target@1 if on main (don't edit their files). Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI (get suggestions, reset, pin).
- s6 Tests (ranking math, context keys, when-conditions, reset, destructive never top), phone + desktop screenshots, UI Review item, report `_claude/builds/reports/smart-menus.md`, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 1 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice, before start): dynamic SECTIONS, not the whole menu
Don't make the whole menu dynamic. Each context menu keeps its normal fixed items in their fixed order (muscle memory). Add dynamic SECTIONS on top of that:
- A 'Suggested' section at the top (learned/predicted items, 3-5, per s2) - can be turned off.
- A context section (items that only apply to this target/state, per s1 'when' conditions), clearly grouped.

- **Every toolbar carries its OWN settings** (stored per toolbar id, synced via axHub like other settings): theming and colours (tokens/assets only: colour theme, style, background, button style, icon/label size, spacing, rounded/flat, opacity), layout (position, orientation, wrap vs scroll vs overflow menu, show/hide, auto-hide), behaviour (double-tap override for this toolbar, tooltips), and its button list.
- **Context-menu hooks on every toolbar** (right-click / long-press): 'Toolbar settings' (that toolbar's own settings), 'Edit toolbar' (opens the Toolbar editor), 'All toolbars...' (Toolbars plugin page that lists and controls every toolbar in the app). Contributed as runtime context items, so every existing and future toolbar gets them; CI check fails any toolbar without them.

### Toolbar editor
- Opens from the toolbar context menu. Add / remove / reorder / group / separators, edit each button (label, icon, tooltip text, action/hook, colour, visibility by level/role, keyboard shortcut), reset to default, undo/redo, live preview, save as an asset so it's hot-swappable and shareable.

### Drag and drop hooks anywhere
- A **hook** = any actionable thing in the app (menu item, nav item, toolbar button, banner item, 'Go to it' hooks, plugin commands from control@1 / plugin-commands-auto, settings pages, screens). - Drag any hook from anywhere and drop it on a **drop target**: any toolbar, the navigation menu, the banners, application menus, context menus, Home. Drag a button from one toolbar to another; nav menu -> toolbar and toolbar -> nav menu.
- On drop: a **configure dialog that depends on where it's dropped** (toolbar = new button dialog; nav menu = nav item dialog; banner = banner item dialog; menu = menu item dialog), prefilled with default values from the hook (label, icon, action, tooltip), with all the options for that target. Confirm creates it; move vs copy choice (default: copy from menus, move between toolbars), undo.
- Make it a framework contract: `drop-target@1` (what it accepts + which configure dialog) and `hook@1` (draggable action descriptor), open registries so any plugin/app can add targets and hooks without kernel changes. Phone: long-press to pick up, drag with edge auto-scroll, drop zones highlight.
- **Banners:** only add the banner drop target through the generic contract. Do NOT merge or rewrite banner-pack (#251), banner-editor (#254) or banners-one work; Brett is reviewing those himself. Note any overlap in the report.
- Rules: add to shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'Every toolbar is a Toolbars plugin toolbar: per-toolbar settings + editor via its context menu, tap-to-confirm on touch only, accepts dropped hooks.' Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI.
